rv.q: Under David R. Gammons’ quick fire direction, CST’s production is astonishingly well executed and the perfect Pride month tribute to Ludlam’s specific genius.

Central Square Theater’s fantastically entertaining production is helmed by David R. Gammons (previous CST directing credits include Vanity Fair and Frankenstein ) who directs Melendy and Graetz with the specificity and finesse of a world-class choreographer.
This production, with David R. Gammons doing double duty as director and scenic designer, is a giddy, irreverent sprint.
The play bear-hugs the penny dreadful genre, with homages to creature features of Victorian vampires, mummies, werewolves, departed former wives and more.
The best part of the production is watching Graetz and Melendy when their technique and commitment to craft are on full display.

Ludlam’s creation of a script that could keep an audience laughing and engaged nearly 40 years after his death suggests that he did, after all, emerge the victor in his own struggle against mortality.
Graetz and Melendy supply nearly all the fuel this production needs to take glorious flight.
This production is funny and two great actors performing this campy gothic mystery made me laugh anyway.
As a master class in acting, it worked.

cn.t: Critics praise this campy production as a hilarious, frenetic romp, with Graetz and Melendy delivering inexhaustible performances through rapid costume changes and nonstop physical comedy in Ludlam's absurdist gothic pastiche.
